summary.title: [Supplements] Touch activation immediately closes evidence popovers
summary.one_line_description: A real touchscreen tap opens an evidence popover on focus and then closes it again in the click handler.

bug_1.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/features/supplements/enhance.ts - function: `enhanceSupplementExplorer`, Lines 89-98 and 142-155 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/e2e/calculator-supplement-comprehensive.spec.ts - test: `all visible supplement badges have exact metrics and every evidence popover opens in view`, Lines 262-324

issue_description.description: Touch input does not pass through the pointer-hover path that records the trigger in `openedByFocus`. A touchscreen tap first focuses the button, so `handleFocusIn` opens the panel. The following click then reaches the default `togglePopover` branch and closes it. A rendered Chromium reproduction with `hasTouch: true` and `badge.tap()` left `aria-expanded="false"` and the controlled panel hidden. The existing badge matrix uses mouse-style `click()` in a desktop Chromium context, so it does not exercise this event sequence. Keep one explicit touch activation state transition so the tap leaves the panel open.
issue_description.expected_vs_actual: | Aspect | Expected | Actual | |--------|----------|--------| | **Touch activation** | One tap opens the controlled evidence panel | Focus opens the panel, then click immediately closes it | | **ARIA state** | `aria-expanded="true"` after the tap | `aria-expanded="false"` after the tap | | **User impact** | Touch users can read and dismiss evidence help | Evidence help never remains visible after a normal tap |

summary.title: [Sharing] A throwing legacy copy API bypasses failure feedback and safe navigation
summary.one_line_description: If `document.execCommand('copy')` throws, the copy-link handler rejects before it can show failure feedback or use the total-failure navigation fallback.

bug_2.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/scripts/social-share.ts - functions: `copyText` and copy-link click handler, Lines 4-24 and 36-48 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/e2e/ui-parity.spec.ts - test: `reopened article endings restore share, comment, disclaimers, wrapping, and floating rail`, Lines 727-768

issue_description.description: The Clipboard API rejection is caught, but the retained `document.execCommand('copy')` call is not. Browsers and constrained document contexts may throw from this deprecated API instead of returning `false`. In that case, the async click listener rejects before setting `data-copied`, before changing the tooltip to `Copy Failed`, and before reaching `location.assign(link.href)`. A focused browser reproduction with a rejected Clipboard API and a throwing `execCommand` produced the page error `exec blocked`, retained the unchanged `Copy Link` label, and performed no fallback navigation. Catch the legacy API exception and convert it into the same explicit total-failure result as a `false` return.
issue_description.expected_vs_actual: | Aspect | Expected | Actual | |--------|----------|--------| | **Total copy failure** | Show `Copy Failed`, clean up the temporary field, then use the safe URL fallback | An uncaught exception aborts the handler | | **Feedback** | The visitor receives a visible failure state | The tooltip remains `Copy Link` | | **Navigation fallback** | The canonical page URL is used only after both copy paths fail | No fallback occurs when the legacy API throws |

summary.title: [Supplements] Server-rendered unfiltered content assigns unsupported evidence badges
summary.one_line_description: Without JavaScript, all 19 supplements render with evidence labels even though no goal filter is selected.

bug_3.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/components/SupplementExplorer.astro - supplement filter and badge markup, Lines 10-13 and 28-39 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/features/supplements/enhance.ts - function: `enhanceSupplementExplorer`, Lines 165-167 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/e2e/calculator-supplement-comprehensive.spec.ts - test: `every supplement filter matches the audited membership, order, TOC, and selected state`, Lines 218-260

issue_description.description: The server output marks every filter `aria-pressed="false"`, renders every supplement, and fills each badge from the record's first evidence entry. Evidence level is category-specific, so the first entry is not a valid label without a selected goal context. JavaScript later applies Muscle Growth and corrects or hides badges, but JavaScript-disabled users and the pre-enhancement document see 19 visible badges with no selected filter. A JavaScript-disabled browser reproduction returned zero pressed filters, 19 visible sections, and 19 visible evidence badges. Render badges without a visible level until enhancement establishes a goal context, while retaining all semantic supplement content.
issue_description.expected_vs_actual: | Aspect | Expected | Actual | |--------|----------|--------| | **Unfiltered state** | No evidence badge appears without a selected goal | Every supplement shows its first category-specific evidence level | | **JavaScript disabled** | Complete supplement content remains usable without misleading filter context | All 19 records show potentially unrelated evidence labels | | **Initial render** | The server contract agrees with the active filter state | Buttons report no selection while badges imply a selection |

summary.title: [Metadata] Supplement route registry disagrees with the rendered description
summary.one_line_description: The configured source-of-truth description for `/supplements/` differs from the description emitted by the page and social metadata.

bug_4.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/config/routes.ts - `/supplements/` route entry, Lines 99-107 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/pages/supplements/index.astro - `BaseLayout` metadata props, Lines 8-14 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro - metadata rendering, Lines 18-28 and 33-50 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/e2e/routes.spec.ts - generated route contract, Lines 10-21

issue_description.description: The route registry defines the supplement description as `A supplement stack distilled from scientific research.`, while the route passes a different, longer description directly to `BaseLayout`. The browser therefore emits the longer value in `meta[name="description"]`, `og:description`, and `twitter:description`, but any registry consumer receives the shorter value. The general route contract test checks only that titles are non-empty and does not compare descriptions, so this divergence remains green. Use one approved description from the route metadata owner and have the supplement page consume it rather than duplicating a second value.
issue_description.code_example:
```typescript # File: src/config/routes.ts, Lines 99-105
{ path: '/supplements/', title: 'The Best Muscle Building Supplement Stack (Based on Research) | Muscle Hacking', description: 'A supplement stack distilled from scientific research.', indexable: true, } ```
```astro # File: src/pages/supplements/index.astro, Lines 8-13
<BaseLayout title="The Best Muscle Building Supplement Stack (Based on Research) | Muscle Hacking" description="Amplify your muscle growth with a curated supplement stack, distilled from 10+ years of scientific research. Gain muscle, lose the confusion." canonicalPath="/supplements/" /> ```
issue_description.expected_vs_actual: | Aspect | Expected | Actual | |--------|----------|--------| | **Metadata source** | Route registry and rendered route use one approved description | Registry and rendered page hold different descriptions | | **Rendered metadata** | Registry consumers predict `description`, Open Graph, and Twitter values | Browser values cannot be derived from the route registry | | **Regression coverage** | Route contract fails when metadata diverges | The generated test checks only a non-empty title and canonical URL |
